title: Failed New York trip, teeth trouble and Nashville
summary: Joe went to New York with no job waiting; the band did poorly and Ory and others left. Gum disease damaged his playing and he worked in Nashville under contract troubles, during the Depression.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Is that Paul Barbrun? Do you remember? Paul Barbrun. Paul Barbrun also. He was playing on drums then. Yes. And they played around New York for a long time. They did fairly well but not much because men began to get tired and Ory was there too. He began to spit. He began to leave Joe. Because he wasn't so strong anymore and all that traveling around and disappointment and all. And Joe was quite disappointed.
I heard once that Joe had some trouble with his teeth about that time. Is that true?

I'm coming along to that time. Then his teeth was getting bad. He was in New York. Then he thought he'd take the roll. Here and there. A little nightstand. And of course all the time the teeth was giving him trouble. And he was failing on the coronet. Was he losing his teeth or just? Piree of the gums. Piree. Piree of the gums. And he went to Nashville, Tennessee on a little job. Well then that's where he made his mistake. He began to go down. His teeth began to get bad and all. And he played for a long time around Nashville. But nothing to it. Nothing to it. You see? The contracts called for so many men being on the job, setting such an hour. And if he wasn't there, the band was so highly responsible. Because Joe had all the fellas got along together. But they wasn't up to par. They didn't realize what they were going to lose. And they did lose the band. And Joe stayed in Nashville quite a while. I went over there. But there was nothing to that.
That was the depression too. Those years. Yes it was. Very, very hard. Very, very hard. We did have a little money. We lost it all at Chicago Bank.
